# Meant Lang

> Meant Lang is a small, checkable language for how an application should behave: who can act, under what conditions, and what changes. People decide the behavior, coding agents draft the model, and the deterministic `meant` toolkit checks it. Engineers choose the implementation.

Developer preview, MIT license. Requires Bun 1.4 or later. Model files use the `.meant` extension, or ```` ```meant ```` fences in Markdown.

## Start from your codebase

Install the CLI:

```
bun add -g meant-lang
```

Then give your coding agent one prompt that names one workflow:

```
Run `meant` and follow its instructions to build a Meant model of the <workflow> workflow in this app.
```

The agent reads its modeling instructions from the CLI, mines that workflow's code into `.meant/model.meant`, proposes vocabulary with file:line evidence for your verdict, and runs check, sim and report. You review the model, its falsified claims, and its open questions.

## Docs

- [Documentation](https://meantlang.dev/docs/): your first model, working with an agent, what verification covers
- [Start from your codebase](https://meantlang.dev/docs/#from-code): install, the one prompt, what the agent does, what you review
- [Command and language reference](https://meantlang.dev/docs/reference/): check, sim, report, fmt, skill, spec, hook
- [Example: sending an invoice](https://meantlang.dev/examples/invoicing/): a complete model with recorded results

## Agent references

- [Modeling instructions](https://meantlang.dev/skill.md): the output of `meant skill`
- [Normative grammar](https://meantlang.dev/spec.md): the output of `meant spec --all`
- [Example model](https://meantlang.dev/examples/invoicing.meant)
- [Recorded simulation of the example](https://meantlang.dev/examples/invoicing.result.json): `meant sim --json` output
- [Everything above in one file](https://meantlang.dev/llms-full.txt)
